title: Public audiences: anonymous readers subscribe, confirm, manage and leave by email
description:
**Goal.** As an anonymous reader of a publication, I subscribe by email to the lists I choose, confirm from my inbox, change my choices and leave from any message, and the host keeps proof of my consent. Papyrus PPY-1081ad (epic PPY-824c14); Papyrus pages PPY-f361ee. Design: docs/public-audiences.md. Covers the public parts of kanbus-eedbbd, kanbus-1c3618, kanbus-ff4727 and kanbus-98e489.

**Not included.** Sign-in subscription, consent per language, digests, Slack and Discord readers.

```gherkin
Feature: Public audiences
  Anonymous readers subscribe to a host's lists by email with double opt-in,
  manage their choices by signed links, and leave in one click.

  Scenario: Double opt-in
    Given a host with a public list "stories"
    When a reader subscribes with the form's own consent wording
    Then they are told to check their email and exactly one confirmation is queued
    And nothing else reaches them until they confirm

  Scenario: The answer reveals nothing
    Given an address already confirmed for "stories"
    When someone subscribes it again
    Then the answer is the same "check your email" and nothing is sent

  Scenario: Consent evidence matches the form
    When a reader confirms
    Then the consent record holds the wording hash, the form, the page path, the origin and both times
    And a subscribe whose wording differs from the form's is refused

  Scenario: A confirmation bomb
    Given a confirmation for an address is still outstanding
    When the address is submitted again and again
    Then no second confirmation is sent until the learned resend gap has passed

  Scenario: The resend gap is learned
    Given at least 59 readers confirmed, almost all within ten minutes
    Then the resend gap is the 95% upper bound of their 95th percentile lag

  Scenario: A network far above what readers do
    Given the host's readers send about one signup per network per hour
    When one network sends far more
    Then further signups from it are told to slow down and nothing is sent

  Scenario: A domain that takes no mail
    When a reader subscribes an address whose domain has no mail server
    Then they are told the address is not valid and nothing is sent

  Scenario: Preferences
    Given a confirmed subscriber of "stories" and "weekly" follows the manage link
    When they turn "weekly" off
    Then a "weekly" event reaches them no more and a "stories" event still does

  Scenario: One-click unsubscribe
    When a mail provider posts the one-click unsubscribe from a message
    Then the reader is unsubscribed in that request and the key stays suppressed
    And every public message carries List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post

  Scenario: Re-subscribing by manage link
    Given a reader who unsubscribed from everything
    When they turn a list on from the manage link
    Then they are subscribed without a new confirmation and a manage_link consent is recorded

  Scenario: Bounces and complaints
    When SES reports a permanent bounce or a complaint for a reader
    Then they are suppressed and unsubscribed from every list

  Scenario: Erasure
    When an admin erases a reader
    Then the address, choices, consent and delivery history are gone
    And an import cannot bring the address back, though the person may subscribe again by the form

  Scenario: Export
    When an admin exports a reader
    Then they get the profile, lists, consent records with wording and delivery history

  Scenario: Import without re-confirming
    When a host imports a confirmed subscriber with their original evidence
    Then they are subscribed with the evidence marked migrated and no mail is sent
    And importing again changes nothing

  Scenario: Fan-out by list
    Given readers subscribed to two lists
    When an event names both lists
    Then each confirmed reader gets exactly one delivery, page by page
```
